nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Soil health management|Soil organic matter enhancement_qna_000
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What is the origin of a large fraction of particulate organic matter (POM)?
nodes.answer: A large fraction of POM originates from roots.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Soil health management|Soil organic matter enhancement_qna_001
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What historical observations contributed to the theory of using biochar for soil fertility and crop yield?
nodes.answer: The theory of using biochar to increase soil fertility and crop yield was introduced based on observations made on Amazonian Black Earth, also known as terra preta.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Soil health management|Soil organic matter enhancement_qna_002
nodes.label: Taxonomy
nodes.question: How do particulate organic matter (POM) fragments contribute to denitrification activity in soil?
nodes.answer: POM fragments provide large amounts of labile carbon that promote local oxygen consumption in microsites, affecting their aeration status compared to the surrounding soil matrix.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Soil health management|Soil organic matter enhancement_qna_003
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What changes occurred in organic carbon levels during the extreme drought-heatwave event?
nodes.answer: There were increases in organic carbon and labile organic carbon contents during the event.
